newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says digital handset share rose.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says digital handset share rose.

text.p: The proportion of digital handsets in Nokia Oy's mobile phone sales, already near 60 percent in full-year 1996, rose further in the first quarter over the year 1996 level, a Nokia spokesman said on Monday.
"The digital share has continued to increase," chief spokesman Lauri Kivinen said by telephone, but gave no figures.
He said digital as a part of overall mobile phone sales remained below the level at Ericsson, because Nokia meets all industry standards.
The world-leading system is analogue AMPS (Advanced Mobile Phone Service) system developed in the U.S.

Kivinen declined to comment on Nokia's handset market share in the first quarter, but noted that in its results statement, the company said it would continue to build on its position as world number one digital mobile phone supplier.
